etymologies.etymologyHTML: From deaf +‎ -en (verbal suffix), compare Middle English deven, deaven (“to make deaf”), Old English ādēafian (“to deafen”), Dutch verdoven (“to stupefy, deafen”), German betäuben (“to stun, stupefy, deafen”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make deaf, either temporarily or permanently.
(transitive, rare, dialectal, sometimes figurative) To stun, as with noise.

quote.citation: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:
quote.text: Racine left the ground  […]  deafened, dazzled and tired to death.
